title: Targeted Radiotheranostics: Bench to Bedside
text:
Reliable tools for earlier diagnosis of malignancies, assessing extent of disease and monitoring response to
treatment, and targeted therapies are critical to improving patient outcomes. I have dedicated 20+ years of my
scientific career to Dr. Sutcliffe’s lab (unit director) developing radiolabeled diagnostic imaging and therapeutic
agents resulting in 3 novel radiopharmaceuticals that are currently under clinical evaluation. I remain
committed to advancing the field of radiotheranostics, refining radiolabeling protocols for wide-spread
application, supporting clinical trials, and to collaboratively advancing new targeted theranostic peptide-
conjugates for cancer-specific therapy.

title: Identifying strategies to reveal genetic results over the lifespan
text: If healthy babies are sequenced near birth, should the underlying data be kept “on file” to inform a lifetime of care, and, if so, what could and should this look like? This research will determine the feasibility of different strategies, analyze their ethical, legal and social implications, understand parents' preferences, and seek consensus on the features of a preferred strategy. The project will generate concrete recommendations for implementers of newborn sequencing and will hence help ensure the ethical rollout of genomic medicine for all.

title: Targeting death receptor pathways to enhance MET-CAR T cell therapy in glioblastoma
text:
Overexpression of MET oncogene is common in glioblastoma (GBM) patients and is highly relevant to treatment
resistance. We have developed novel MET-targeting CAR T cells selectively inhibiting MET-positive tumors in
preclinical tumor models. In this application, we will implement radiation with MET-CAR T cell therapy to improve
the potency. If successful, this study will provide a new MET-targeting approach to overcome GBM
heterogeneity.

title: Role of RMTg afferents in mechanisms of withdrawal from chronic ethanol exposure
text:
The neurobiological mechanisms underlying symptoms of withdrawal are poorly understood despite the fact that
they serve as potent triggers for relapse in individuals attempting to remain abstinent from alcohol. While our
recent work uncovered a role for the rostromedial tegmental nucleus (RMTg) in regulating withdrawal symptoms,
the broader neural circuitry that governs this effect remains unknown. The proposed project will interrogate the
mechanistic involvement of input from the lateral habenula to the RMTg in symptoms of withdrawal and in doing
so provide an opportunity to identify new potential therapeutic targets for the development of drugs to treat
withdrawal symptoms.

title: Spatial functional genomics to identify regulators of the tumor microenvironment and cancer immunity
text:
The objective of this project is to determine the genes regulating tumor composition and facilitating tumor growth
and resistance to immunity & immunotherapy, with the goal of identifying factors that can be targeted to enhance
tumor immunity and improve cancer treatment. We will focus on four highly prevalent and deadly cancers - non
small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), high grade serous ovarian cancer
(HGSOC), and oral squamous cell carcinomas (OSCC), and utilize large-scale genomic and transcriptomic data
from patient tumors, spatial functional genomics, and computational analysis, to reach our goal.

title: Transcriptome reprogramming in the early embryo
text:
This proposal aims to uncover how chromosome regulation during early animal development underlies the
gene expression programs necessary to generate embryonic stem cells. The mechanisms underlying how
specific genes are activated while others are repressed to achieve stemness are still not fully understood.
However, deciphering this regulation is especially important for biomedical efforts to treat disorders of cell
identity such as cancer, as well as for improving the capacity to artificially induce stem cells for disease
modeling and personalized therapies.

title: Developing and Evaluating Multi-Modal Clinical Diagnostic Reasoning Models for Automated Diagnosis Generation
text:
Busy hospital settings and information overload from the electronic health record (EHR) contribute to decisional
shortcuts and biases by clinicians that lead to missed opportunities for timely and accurate diagnoses. The
proposal aims to develop novel clinical natural language processing (NLP) models that learn and integrate multi-
modal EHR data, conduct reasoning over a large-scale medical knowledge base, and test them in a clinical
decision support system to mitigate diagnostic error. Completion of the aims will inform the development of NLP-
driven clinical decision support tools that generate accurate diagnoses to overcome provider heuristics and
improve patient outcomes.

title: Amyloid clearing therapy in dementia with Lewy bodies plus Alzheimers disease (ACT DLB+)
text:
This project aims to support the investigation of new treatments for Dementia with Lewy bodies by conducting
a phase 2 multi-site double blind clinical trial using an amyloid antibody, donanemab, while collecting and
sharing benchmark data from the trial and post-trial observational period with the greater scientific community.
By successfully completing this research, we will determine whether treating people with Dementia with Lewy
bodies with concomitant Alzheimer’s disease with donanemab is safe and efficacious, determine whether
donanemab would be suitable for a phase 3 trial in this population, and create a data library of longitudinal
biomarker, imaging, and clinical data of diverse representation of this cohort of which relatively minimal data
exists. This approach will enable a critical step in discovering treatment for patients with Dementia with Lewy
bodies and Alzheimer’s disease where there are currently none.

title: Chemical Approaches to Understand O-GlcNAc Glycosylation and Its Roles in Neurodegeneration
text:
This research seeks to understand how O-GlcNAc (O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine) glycosylation, an
essential, abundant posttranslational modification of proteins, contributes to the onset and progression of
Alzheimer’s disease and other related dementias. The insights gained will further our understanding of how
specific changes in O-GlcNAc glycosylation regulate cellular functions and drive toxic aggregation of proteins
that are hallmarks of these diseases. A major goal is to reveal new targets for therapeutic intervention.

title: Decoding Mechanisms and Signaling by an S-acylated isoform of Calcineurin
text:
Disruptions in calcium and lipid signaling contribute to a wide range of human diseases, including metabolic
disorders, cardiovascular disease, and neurodegeneration. This research will uncover how reversible lipid
modifications regulate membrane-associated enzymes like calcineurin to maintain precise spatial control of
calcium signaling. By revealing new principles of signal integration at membranes, these studies may inform
therapeutic strategies targeting lipid-modified proteins involved in disease.

title: Retroviral infection and new modulators of the MHCII pathway
text:
Understanding of how H2-O, a non-classical Major Histocompatibility Class II (MHCII)-like molecule, H2-O,
negatively regulates MHCII antigen presentation will undoubtedly improve current vaccination protocols and
may facilitate vaccination against pathogens for which vaccines are not currently available.

title: Towards Interpretable Imaging-based Gastric Cancer Prognosis via Prototypical and Attentional Deep Learning
text:
It is currently estimated that up to around 30% of patients diagnosed with gastric cancer are over- or under-
treated, sustaining substantial morbidities from unnecessary side-effects or treatment failures. Our proposal
focuses on developing innovative deep learning methods with intrinsic interpretability to analyze radiology and
pathology images, enhancing the model's generalizability and clinical applicability, while providing valuable
information to complement the current clinical staging system. Ultimately, effectively integrating radiology and
pathology imaging with the current clinicopathological markers could enable more informed, precision-
medicine, treatment decisions to reduce unnecessary side-effects while improving long-term outcomes for
patients diagnosed with gastric cancer.

title: Molecular factors controlling vitamin A uptake homeostasis
text:
Understanding the mechanisms that regulate vitamin A homeostasis has significant potential for reducing
vitamin A deficiencies and addressing metabolic disorders such as obesity and diabetes. Insights from this
research may guide the development of nutritional guidelines and therapeutic strategies to optimize vitamin A
supply and status, thereby enhancing metabolic health and reducing the global burden of associated diseases.

title: Brain structure and function and the CNS HIV reservoir in older people living with HIV
text:
Aging-associated comorbidities, such as neurocognitive impairment (NCI), among people living with HIV (PWH)
can lead to high morbidity, mortality and healthcare costs. HIV may persist in the brain despite adequate viral
suppression in blood with antiretroviral treatment. Our overall goal in this proposal is to disentangle the effects
of HIV viral replication within the brain, inflammation, alterations in brain structure and function that impact NCI
in PWH by determining if the impacts of brain functional connectivity deficits, neuroinflammation,
neurodegeneration or greater white matter hyperintensity volume are mediated by CNS HIV viral persistence.

title: Mechanisms of visual transduction and light-driven behaviors in Aedes aegypti
text:
The mosquito disease vector, Aedes aegypti, is troubling because it spreads viruses that cause diseases
such as dengue, yellow fever, and Zika, which infect >100,000,000 people/year. Once this daytime biting
mosquito senses CO2 from our breadth, they then home in on people using visual and other cues. Despite the
importance of vision in finding humans, our understanding of the visual mechanisms that mosquitoes use to
find people are largely unknown. The goal of this application is to fill this gap. This project lays the conceptual
foundation for devising innovative approaches to limit the ability of mosquitoes in detecting hosts for blood
meals.

title: A National Test of a Culturally Tailored mHealth Integrated Smoking Cessation and Mental Health Intervention for Black Adults with HIV
text: African American/Black (hereafter referred to as Black) adults with HIV/AIDS who smoke constitute a disparities group for poorer smoking cessation outcomes, mental health outcomes, and HIV disease outcomes. To help address this public health issue, our team developed a tailored, adapted, highly accessible, and integrated smartphone application that aims to increase smoking cessation, promote mental well-being, and improve HIV outcomes among Black adults with HIV/AIDS who smoke, which we now seek to test in a large-scale, nationwide trial.

title: Core 2: Pilot Project Core
text: Project Summary – Pilot Projects The goals of this Pilot Projects Core of the VCU Alcohol Research Center (ARC) are to: 1) manage the progress and quality control for our two designated initial pilot projects, 2) solicit and evaluate future pilot grant proposals to further expand the scientific breadth of VCU-ARC, 3) encourage pilot grant awardees to submit proposals for independent funding and 4) support training opportunities for students and postdoctoral fellows within laboratories of funded pilot projects. The first proposed Pilot Project is entitled “Investigating the relationship between alcohol use, blood pressure phenotypes, and genetics” and will be led by Dr. Elvin Price, a clinical pharmacologist and translational researcher with extensive training in pharmacogenomics. He will determine if tag SNPs in VCU-ARC genes of interest impact drinking behaviors and cardiovascular disease phenotypes in a local cohort recruited from the community through the established Translational Approaches to Personalized Health (TAPH) study. This project will interact with Project 1, led by Dr. Michael F. Miles, and Project 3, led by Dr. Amy Lasek. Pilot Project 1 will also interface with the human genetics studies proposed in Projects 4 (Dr. Dick) and 5 (Drs. Riley, Bacanu, and Nguyen) as new genes influencing the risk for AUD are identified. The second targeted pilot, entitled “Assess the influence of select dynamic non-SNV genomic variation on AUD risk and alcohol related outcomes using existing biobank resources including UK Biobank and All of Us” will be conducted by Dr. B. Todd Webb, an expert in using statistical genetics, bioinformatics, and computational genomic tools to understand the genetic architecture of complex human diseases such as AUD. He will focus on the role of telomere length and mitochondrial abundance as indices of dynamic variation in AUD-related phenotypes. Project 2 will interface with Projects 4 and 5. We will solicit other proposals in year 2 and fund the two best of them in years 3-4, then solicit proposals again in year 4 to fund one in year 5. The pilot program is an important component of the VCU-ARC that will enable us to attract new and innovative researchers to interact with Center investigators and expand high quality alcohol research at VCU.

title: Systems biological assessment of vaccination-induced protective immunity in African children
text:
The most advanced malaria vaccine candidate, RTS,S, only provides partial and rapidly waning efficacy
against malaria in young children. The immunological mechanisms underlying this suboptimal response remain
mysterious, and in this proposal we will utilize a systems biological approach to delineate the molecular
networks that drive such responses.

title: Multimodal Molecular Imaging Platforms for Cancer Discovery and Translation
text:
My career goal is to make the most of my unique role at the Biophotonics Research Center and
Molecular Imaging Center. I aim to become a national leader in developing multimodal molecular
imaging platforms that aid cancer discovery and translation. I believe this path will enable me to
make significant contributions to substantial advancements in biomedical science. I will achieve
this by proactively developing and deploying integrated technology platforms that utilize novel
imaging probes and major instrumentation, such as multimodality, multispectral, and
hyperspectral systems, to create standardized AI-based image analysis pipelines and shared
cloud databases. My goal is to turn these platforms into valuable, scalable resources that serve
the Siteman Cancer Center and the broader research community. With the support of this R50
award, I look forward to accelerating the process of translating fundamental scientific discoveries
into real-world clinical solutions, which will help improve cancer diagnosis, treatment, and patient
care.

title: Dissecting temporal and spatial dynamics of immunotherapy resistance
text:
Immunotherapy is now first line treatment in recurrent or metastatic head and neck cancer, yet the majority of
patients do not respond. The proposed research aims to elucidate how the composition and spatial architecture
of the head and neck cancer tumor immune microenvironment impacts response to immunotherapy, and how it
changes across time following immunotherapy exposure. This knowledge is critical to improve treatment
selection, develop new therapeutics and ultimately, improve survival outcomes for patient suffering from Head
and Neck Cancer.
